title: Mass Revocation Event

containment: Throttle revocation processing to prevent cascade
Activate fleet-wide revocation pause if rate exceeds 500/min
Snapshot current revocation state before further processing
investigation: Identify revocation source (automated policy vs manual operator action)
Audit revocation requests for unauthorized or anomalous patterns
Check whether revocation trigger was a compromised signing key
Determine blast radius: how many nodes and delegations are affected
repair: If revocations are legitimate, resume processing at controlled rate
If revocations are illegitimate, restore the durable trust-card registry store from verified backup snapshot
Re-issue trust delegations for incorrectly revoked entities
If a signing key is compromised, follow the governed signer-config and evidence-ledger rotation procedure; this release exposes no CLI key-rotation subcommand
Use franken-node trust revoke --publisher-public-key <pubkey-path> --json to revoke all artifacts signed by a compromised publisher key
Update revocation policy to prevent recurrence
verification: Confirm revocation list consistency across all fleet nodes
Validate that legitimate revocations are honored fleet-wide
Verify that incorrectly revoked entities have restored access

For any key-rotation emergency, verify that the applied signer-config and evidence-ledger entries identify the old key, new key, approval trace, and rotation timestamp before considering remediation complete
Run trust delegation audit via franken-node trust scan --deep --audit --json
rollback: Restore pre-revocation trust state from snapshot
Coordinate fleet-wide epoch reset if full rollback needed
Escalate to governance board if policy-level changes required

drill_scenario: Simulate mass revocation by issuing 200 test revocations against a staging fleet. Verify that rate-limiting engages, containment procedures activate, and selective rollback restores test delegations correctly.
